responses.text: Write-up only; no Lean or condition changed. The README now says the benchmark's launches are not covered. Every one runs after proton.start(..., hook="triton") (line 756) has installed Triton's launch and kernel-load hooks, and proton.deactivate() (lines 501, 757) leaves them installed until proton.finalize() (line 764). That covers the warm-up launches (line 484) and the timed ones (line 492), which puts them outside Compiler.Faithful's scope point 3 (part (B); exclusions.md, 'a hook'). The claim covers the test's launch (line 749, made before line 756) and launches of the benchmark's sizes (M = N = 8192, K a positive multiple of 128 up to 2^14) made with no hook installed. Changed: the introduction, Conditions ('Which of the host's launches are covered', the part (A) preamble, the point-4 and point-9 bullets, the part (B) paragraph) and a new Narrowings bullet, with the environment bullet updated.

Same point as F1; write-up only. Inst.ok still covers M = N = 8192 with K a positive multiple of 128 up to 2^14, so no condition changes. The README no longer counts the benchmark's launches as the script makes them among the covered launches. In Conditions ('Which of the host's launches are covered'), the part (A) preamble, the point-9 bullet, the part (B) paragraph and a new Narrowings bullet it says: the benchmark's launches run with proton's launch hooks installed (proton.start(..., hook="triton"), line 756, removed only by proton.finalize(), line 764), outside scope point 3, so they are not covered. The claim covers the test's launch (line 749) and launches of the benchmark's sizes made with no hook installed, for instance bench_block_scaled without the profiling session of lines 755-765. On the non-blocking remark: I keep K <= 2^14 so that the tolerance stays meaningful at every covered K (the closed form's 0.4% of sum|p|, closed_rel_le, is proved for K <= 2^14). The README's Narrowings now say the proof itself needs only the int32 bounds and the room condition.
